paper.title_en: A Hopf Algebraic Theory of the Quantum Magnusian
paper.abstract_en: We develop a Hopf-algebraic theory of graph coefficients arising in the quantum Magnus expansion. At the classical level, the expansion is governed by directed trees, whereas its quantum counterpart involves loop graphs, multiple edges, and several types of edge data. We introduce a contraction Hopf algebra of mixed quivers containing these diagrams and closed under contraction. On this algebra we define a character $e$ from normalized linear-extension data, directed-tadpole factors, and a prescription for undirected edges, and let $ω$ be its convolution inverse. Our main result is a universal closed formula for the connected function $ω_c$ on every finite mixed quiver, expressed as a finite sum over ordered set partitions of the vertices. We also construct a weighted vertex-splitting Hopf structure on the unlocalized mixed-quiver algebra, with convolution $\star_V$ and canonical edge-weight character $ζ_V$, such that $ω_c=\log_{\star_V}ζ_V$. Compatibility of the two coproducts and an explicit identity between their characters explain this equality. We further prove that the two-vertex contraction identity, tadpole factorization, vanishing on disconnected graphs, and boundary data uniquely determine $ω_c$. For acyclic quivers, the formula reduces to a permutation formula with coefficients depending only on descent numbers. We derive this formula independently from the quantum Magnus expansion using operator products and Wick contractions, showing that the physical graph coefficients are governed by the convolution structure of the contraction Hopf algebra. Further consequences include a refined quantum Murua formula and orientation-sum identities related to Tutte and chromatic polynomials.
